name: Drew

biography.name: Drew

background.family: Lives with their mother and grandmother.
background.finances: Modest but steady income; savings and dependable work matter.
background.cultureLanguages: English; extended family frequently asks for help with devices.
background.school: Public high school without a coding course that fits their schedule.
background.accessOpportunities: Library instructions, family devices, and school career advising.

timeline.story: In 2014, Drew enjoyed matching objects to pictures and helping sort kitchen utensils. They liked knowing where things belonged, but also invented sprawling games in which the utensils became vehicles and lost all resemblance to their original purpose.

At six, they began helping a grandparent find familiar television settings. During 2017, Drew learned that trying the same button repeatedly was less useful than remembering what changed after each attempt and asking before changing an unfamiliar setting.

In 2018, Drew liked school science demonstrations when instructions were clear. Mathematics felt comfortable some weeks and difficult others, and comments about naturally gifted classmates made them wonder whether technical interests required a special kind of brilliance.

During 2020, relatives asked Drew to help reconnect devices during online calls. They followed instructions, tested one possible fix at a time, and felt pleased when someone could join the conversation without needing to replace the device.

At twelve, Drew started writing simple notes about successful fixes. In 2023, they explained a connection problem patiently to a relative but still asked an adult to check unfamiliar instructions before attempting changes beyond their experience.

Across 2024 and 2025, Drew remained interested in practical computer support without access to coding classes. They often described new tools as things requiring help, while a teacher encouraged them to separate needing instruction from assuming they could never learn.

At sixteen in 2026, Drew is comparing Texas certificates and college options for practical technology study. They want useful service and steady income, with no assumption that research is the destination or that their worries constitute a diagnosed condition.

avoids: Being told only geniuses can work with technology
demonstratedSkills: Tests one change at a time
ambitions: They imagine a dependable home, growing savings, and ordinary independence near people they trust.

biography.selfDescription: I do not feel like a computer expert, but I like figuring out one small problem at a time. I would rather ask for help and understand what changed than pretend I knew the answer from the start.
